set_aside.subject: sandbox scratch-limit outcome detection
set_aside.text: “The size limit is the host kernel's own: the runner ignores the signal the host sends for a write past it, so the write fails with an error the code can see” together with “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`”
set_aside.question: Which module observes and records that the per-file scratch limit was hit when agent code catches the write error and returns normally, and what observable fact lets it distinguish that hit from an ordinary code-handled write error?
options: The in-sandbox runner records every kernel-reported file-size-limit hit on its protected channel to `sandbox`
The parent or `sandbox` derives the hit from a post-execution file observation
A caught write failure is not considered a detected limit hit, so the execution may otherwise succeed
set_aside.default_guess: Have the in-sandbox runner report the file-size-limit event through its protected channel, with `sandbox` owning the resulting `resource_exhausted` classification.
